These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.

These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.

These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.

These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.

These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.

{1–3} {By the sky containing the constellations}; that is, the sky possessing mansions, which include the mansions of the sun, the moon and the stars, arranged in their courses in the most perfect order and system, which indicates the perfection of God's [Exalted be He] power, mercy, vast knowledge and wisdom. {And the promised Day}: this is the Day of Resurrection, in which God promised creation that He would gather them, bring together their first and last, their farthest and nearest, the Day that cannot change, and God does not break His promise. {And the witness and the witnessed}: this includes everyone who is characterized by this attribute; that is, the seer and the seen, the present and the one present to, the one who witnesses and the one witnessed. The thing sworn to is what this oath contains of God's dazzling signs, manifest wisdoms and wide mercy. It was said that the thing sworn to is His saying:

{4–9} {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}: this is an invocation of destruction upon them. The "ukhdūd" (trench) is the pits dug in the earth. These companions of the trench were disbelieving people, and among them were believing people. They sought to make the believers enter their religion, but the believers refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the earth, cast fire into it, sat around it, tormented the believers and presented them to it. Whoever responded to them they released, and whoever remained steadfast in faith they threw into the fire. This is the utmost of warring against God and His believing party, and for this God cursed them, destroyed them and threatened them. So He said: {Destroyed were the companions of the trench}, then explained the trench with His saying: {The fire, fueled with wood. When they were sitting around it. And they, of what they were doing to the believers, were witnesses}. This is among the greatest forms of tyranny and hardness of heart, for they combined disbelief in God's signs, opposition to them, warring against their people, torturing them with a torment that makes hearts tremble, and their presence at the time of casting them in. Yet they resented in the believers only a quality for which they should be praised and through which their happiness lies: that they believed in {God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy}; that is, the One who possesses the might by which He subdues everything, and who is praiseworthy in His sayings, actions and attributes. {To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth}: in creation and servants, disposing of them as He wills. {And God is, over all things, Witness}: in knowledge, hearing and sight. Did those rebels against Him not fear that the Mighty, the Powerful would seize them? Did they not all know that they are slaves of God, and that no one has authority over another without the permission of the Owner? Or was it hidden from them that God encompasses their deeds and will recompense them for them? No indeed! The disbeliever is in delusion, and the ignorant is in blindness and straying from the right path.

{10} Then He threatened them and promised them, and offered them repentance, saying: {Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the burning}; that is, the severe torment that burns. Al-Ḥasan (may God have mercy on him) said: Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His allies and the people of His obedience, and He calls them to repentance.

{11} When He mentioned the punishment of the wrongdoers, He mentioned the reward of the believers, saying: {Indeed, those who believe}: in their hearts, {and do righteous deeds}: with their limbs, {for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment}: in which they have attained the triumph of God's pleasure and the abode of His honor.

{12} {Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe}; that is, His punishment of the people of great crimes and sins is strong and severe, and He is ever watchful over the wrongdoers. God the Exalted said: {And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe}.

{13} {Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats}; that is, He alone originates creation and restores it; none shares with Him in that.

{14} {And He is the Forgiving}: who forgives all sins for whoever repents, and pardons evil deeds for whoever seeks His forgiveness and turns back in repentance. {the Loving}: whom His beloved love with a love that nothing resembles. Just as nothing resembles Him in the attributes of majesty and beauty, meanings and actions, so His love in the hearts of His chosen creatures, which follows from that, is not like any kind of love. For this reason His love is the root of worship, the love that precedes and overcomes all loves, even if the others are not subordinate to it; it becomes a torment for those who have it. He, the Exalted, is the Loving, the one who loves His beloved, as He said: {He loves them and they love Him}. And wadd (affection) is pure love.
In this there is a subtle secret: He joined "the Loving" with "the Forgiving," to show that when the people of sins repent to God and turn back to Him, He forgives their sins and loves them. It should not be said that He forgives their sins but their affection does not return to them, as some confused people have said. Rather, God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man on his riding-beast, on which were his food, drink and everything that sustains him, which lost him in a deadly desert. He despaired of it and lay down in the shade of a tree, awaiting death. While he was in that state, behold, his riding-beast was standing over his head, and he took hold of its halter. God is greater in joy at the repentance of the servant than this man with his riding-beast, and this is the greatest joy that can be conceived. So to God belong praise, thanks and pure affection. How great is His goodness, how abundant His good, how plentiful His kindness and how vast His bounty!

{15} {Owner of the Throne, the Glorious}; that is, the Lord of the great Throne, whose greatness is such that it encompasses the heavens, the earth and the Kursi; compared with the Throne, they are like a ring thrown into a desert compared with the rest of the earth. God singled out the Throne for mention because of its greatness and because it is the creature nearest to Him [Exalted be He]. In the reading with the genitive (majīd as an adjective of the Throne), this is its description; in the reading with the nominative, it is a description of God. Majd means the breadth and greatness of attributes.

{16} {Effecter of what He intends}; that is, whatever He wills He does. When He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. No one is an effecter of what he wills except God, for creatures, even if they wish something, must have a helper and an obstacle for their will, whereas God has no helper for His will and no one to prevent what He wills.

{17–18} Then He mentioned some of His acts that show the truth of what His messengers brought, saying: {Has there reached you the account of the hosts: of Pharaoh and Thamūd?} And how they denied the messengers, so God made them among the destroyed.

{19} {But those who disbelieve are in denial}; that is, they continue persistently in denial and obstinacy; signs do not benefit them, and admonitions do not avail them.

{20} {And God, from behind them, encompasses}: He has encompassed them in knowledge and power, as in His saying: {Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful}. In this is a severe warning to the disbelievers of punishment from One whom they are in the grip of and under whose management they are.

{21–22} {Rather, it is an honored Qur'an}; that is, vast in its meanings, great, abundant in good and knowledge. {In a preserved tablet}: protected from alteration, addition and omission, and protected from the devils. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded everything. This indicates the sublimity, eloquence and elevated status of the Qur'an with God, Exalted be He. And God knows best.

Finished with its tafsir.
